rule.title: Strict State Separation (Server vs Global UI vs Form State)
rule.statement: Frontend state must be strictly partitioned into Server State (caching API data), Global UI State (Zustand: active modal, sidebar), and Form State (React Hook Form).
rule.rationale: Storing server response arrays in global Zustand stores causes cache invalidation nightmares, stale data, and synchronization bugs.
rule.implementation_guidance: Never copy server API response lists into Zustand. Keep Zustand lean for client-only UI flags.

forbidden.example: Storing documents: Document[] in a global Zustand store and attempting to manually update it on every CRUD operation.

preferred.example: useUIStore: { isSidebarOpen, activeModalId }; useDocuments: fetches and caches server data via API client.

source.book_title: Learn React with TypeScript - Third Edition
source.evidence_quote: Partition state into server state and client state. Do not manage server data in client global state managers without dedicated caching semantics.

rule.title: URL-as-State for Search Queries, Filters, and Pagination
rule.statement: State that alters the primary view of data (search terms, filter categories, sorting order, active pagination page) must be synchronized with URL search parameters.
rule.rationale: Storing search and filter state purely in React useState or global stores breaks browser back/forward navigation, makes bookmarking impossible, and impairs link sharing.
rule.implementation_guidance: Use useSearchParams() and useRouter().replace() with debounce for text inputs. Read parameters server-side in page.tsx for direct Server Component rendering.

forbidden.example: const [page, setPage] = useState(1); const [filter, setFilter] = useState('all'); // State lost on refresh, impossible to bookmark

preferred.example: const searchParams = useSearchParams(); const page = Number(searchParams.get('page')) || 1; function onPageChange(p) { updateUrlParam('page', p); }

source.chapter: Chapter 6: Routing, Navigation, and Search Params
source.section: Deep Linking and Search Parameter State
source.evidence_quote: The URL is the most durable form of state in web applications. Search filters and pagination must be serialized into query parameters to ensure shareability.
